prompt: Nine brownies are shared equally among $4$ friends. How many brownies does each friend get?
hint: Equal sharing is division. The answer here will not be a whole number, so think of the division as a fraction.

hints.text: Equal sharing is division. The answer here will not be a whole number, so think of the division as a fraction.
Write $9 \div 4$ as $\frac{9}{4}$. To see its size, find how many times $4$ goes into $9$ and what is left.
$4$ goes into $9$ twice with $1$ left, so each friend gets $\frac{9}{4}$, or $2\frac{1}{4}$, brownies.

explanation: Sharing $9$ brownies among $4$ friends is $9 \div 4$, which can be written as $\frac{9}{4}$.
To read that as a mixed number, divide: $4$ goes into $9$ twice with $1$ left over.
The leftover brownie is cut into fourths, so each friend gets $2\frac{1}{4}$ brownies.
Check: $4 \times 2\frac{1}{4} = 8 + 1 = 9$ brownies, so each share is $\frac{9}{4}$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Hand them out
steps: Give everyone $2$ whole brownies first — that uses $8$.
One brownie is left, cut into $4$ equal pieces, one piece each.
So each friend has $2$ brownies and $\frac{1}{4}$ more: $2\frac{1}{4}$ ✓
